question: Can the audited parameterized inherited carrier (git blob b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796, sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72) be landed byte-identically at the shipped path src/spider/kernel.py through the sanctioned product promotion path, such that after promotion the shipped execution path contains a concrete parameterized mechanism that an inherited procedure visibly instantiates and executes on a real task, together with a companion known-negative refusal certificate, satisfying B1 and pre-freeze executable-mechanism readiness condition (1)?
hypothesis: Installing the audited carrier bytes byte-identically at src/spider/kernel.py (while preserving the literal distill path and its 0.5 confidence) enables: (a) induction of one parameterized mechanism per (family, resource_type) from training observations on the frozen credential-free localhost HTTP substrate (F1 documents/records, F2 widgets/gadgets; confidence 0.9; slots session_token/property/value/<id>; id-slot support ^<type>\-0[0-9]{2}$); (b) resolution of every held-out novelty-0.0 in-support identifier to EXECUTABLE with correctly bound action whose URL contains the held-out identifier, executing over real HTTP (200, success true) with verify true and no cold fallback; (c) refusal of the three negative constructions (out-of-support identifier, missing required parameter, wrong intent) with bound_action null and correct categorized reason; (d) pre-install discrimination (pre-install bytes over-accept the inputs the carrier refuses); (e) PASS of the frozen synthetic arm-differentiation certificate under the durable install condition.
falsifier: Failure of any of C1-C5 falsifies the hypothesis (C1 real positive < 10/10, C2 real refusal < 30/30 with wrong category/non-null bound_action, C3 pre-install discrimination absent, C4 synthetic certificate not PASS, C5 promotion suite failing). Failures in C6-C10 are MEASUREMENT_INVALID; missing frozen prerequisite or impossible in-scope installation is BLOCKED.
